thread:
olivia: Hey team — quick Q. Trying to add my 23 yo brother to my medical + dental. He's a full-time student at Universidad de Barcelona and moved in with me last month. He doesn't have a US SSN yet. Is the university enrollment letter enough for proof of full-time student status? Is this a QLE (moved in) or do we need a different reason?

maya_peopleops: Hi Olivia — sounds like a QLE (change in household) if he moved into your primary residence. We typically need: proof of relationship, proof of residency (date he moved in), and proof of full-time student status. Foreign enrollment letters are okay if they include term dates and are on school letterhead.

samir_payroll: Adding payroll note — SSN not required for benefits enrollment, but if you want dependent premiums deducted pre-tax or to add on payroll we may need a TIN for certain tax reporting later. We can still enroll him and process deductions; payroll will follow up if tax docs required later.

benefits-bot: Automated note: Please upload all docs via the Benefits Portal (Benefits > Manage Dependents) within 30 days of the QLE. Accepted docs: official enrollment letter, transcript, student schedule, government-issued ID, lease or utility bill for residency. If docs are not in English attach a certified translation.

olivia: Great — thanks. Two follow-ups: 1) Is a student ID + portal screenshot acceptable if the letter is delayed by the school? 2) He only has a Spanish DNI, no US ID.

maya_peopleops: 1) student ID + screenshot can be a temporary supplement but we prefer the official letter for verification. 2) DNI is fine for ID; for relationship proof we need a birth certificate or shared family document showing siblings, or you can submit a short affidavit + supporting docs. If you expect the official enrollment letter within a couple weeks, upload the temporary docs now and swap when you get the letter.

kyle_hradmin: Quick process note — please create a case in the HR portal with "QLE dependent add" and attach what you have. We'll set the event date to the date he moved in. Retro effective coverage is typically the 1st of the month following the event unless there is documentation to support an earlier effective date; benefits team will confirm after doc review.

olivia: OK will open the case now. One more: do dependents studying abroad need an apostille for translations? The university office suggested an apostille for official letters.

maya_peopleops: Apostille not required for most cases. A certified English translation is sufficient. If the document looks unofficial we might ask for additional verification.

samir_payroll: For payroll proration: if added mid-pay-cycle, deductions will be prorated on next paycheck. If you want the premium reflected earlier we'll need the exact move-in date in the case.

olivia: Uploaded student ID, portal screenshot, DNI, and a scanned lease showing move-in date to the HR portal (case #32145). I'll add the official enrollment letter once the university issues it next week.

kyle_hradmin: Got it — I'll mark the case as "pending verification." Folks, I'll review docs and confirm coverage effective date once we get the official letter. If anything is missing I'll update the case. :thumbsup:

maya_peopleops: Thanks Olivia — we'll process and let you know within 5 business days. If you hit any issues, ping us here or email benefits@redwood.com.

olivia: Thank you all! :pray:
